references.text: Abraham's original oath to his servant: He must not take a wife for Isaac from the daughters of Canaan, but go to Abraham's relatives to find a wife.
Esau took wives from among the Canaanite women, which was a source of grief to Isaac and Rebekah.
Isaac commands Jacob not to take a wife from among the Canaanite women, but to go to Paddan-Aram to find a wife there.
Esau realizes that the Canaanite women are not well regarded by his parents, so he takes a wife from among the descendants of Ishmael.
The same event and instruction from Abraham to his servant, where verse 3 is the original oath and verse 37 is the servant's retelling of it.
A thematic parallel showing the continuity of God's requirement to separate from the Canaanites, from Abraham's time until after the exile.
The same instruction is given to the next generation (Jacob), confirming that the prohibition against Canaanite wives is a repeated covenant obligation.
